doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Losing interest in Tatum; playing for show
summary: He found Tatum less interesting over time and thinks such playing, like all public work, is for show.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And there was a lot of scale work and stuff and transpositions and transitions and stuff. But after a while I found him not so interesting as I thought he was.
Tatum. Because of the similarities and how much further can you get out? How much can you get out of that?
Do you think some of it was for show? I mean he had amazing—
Actually, all of it was for show. I mean who would learn how to play like that just for their own self?
In fact everybody out here that’s doing something in the public is doing it for the public not for themselves.
I didn’t study all what I learned — I didn’t study that just to say hey I can do this stuff. Show me. That’s what they want, show me.
